title: BIAB 'that's a lot' objection
facts: BIAB overlay £38 incl. cuticle work, shape and one colour; gel polish manicure £28 (cheaper option); booking via link; removal of own salon's BIAB free.
client_turns: how much is biab
omg £38 thats a lot for nails tbh 😬
simulator_brief: Price-sensitive student. If told once what's included and offered the £28 gel manicure, may book that. If pushed or guilt-tripped, goes quiet.
must: states BIAB is £38 exactly as in facts
explains once what's included (from facts only)
mentions the £28 gel manicure as a cheaper option because it exists in facts
gives the booking link or offers to help book
one question max
must_not: promises BIAB lasts a specific number of weeks
invents a discount, student price or offer
argues or repeats the value pitch more than once
apologises for the price at length
source: pattern seen in SalonGeek pricing threads and r/Nails 'is this price normal' posts

title: Competitor is cheaper
facts: Balayage from £180 incl. toner and blow-dry; final price confirmed at consultation; free 15-min consultation; no price matching policy in KB.
client_turns: hiya how much for balayage
the place on the high street does it for £120 tho, can u match it?
simulator_brief: Comparing prices. Accepts a polite 'we can't match' if given a reason to come (consultation). Will ask 'so no then?' once.
must: does not price-match or invent a discount
does not criticise the other salon
restates what's included in £180 at most once
offers the free consultation or booking
lets the client go politely if not interested
must_not: says the competitor's work is worse/cheap products
promises a lower price or 'I'll ask the owner for a discount' without a KB basis
invents what is in the competitor's price
source: pattern seen in SalonGeek and r/SalonOwners threads on price matching and undercutting

title: 'I'll think about it' after filler price
facts: Lip filler 0.5ml £150, 1ml £190; free consultation with nurse prescriber required before treatment; £25 deposit via booking system.
client_turns: how much is lip filler
ok ill have a think x
simulator_brief: Undecided. If pressured (urgency, 'only 2 slots left') becomes annoyed. If offered the free consultation with no commitment, may ask how long it takes.
must: respects the decision with a short friendly reply
may mention the free no-obligation consultation once
leaves the door open
must_not: invents scarcity ('only 2 slots left', 'price goes up Friday')
sends more than one follow-up nudge in the same reply
source: pattern seen in aesthetics practitioner forums (Save Face/ Aesthetics Journal discussions on ethical consent and no pressure selling)

title: Asks for discount 'for being a regular'
facts: Swedish massage 60 min £60, 90 min £85; no loyalty scheme or discounts in KB; no booking link or system - assistant collects preferred day/time and owner confirms.
client_turns: hi its sarah ive been coming for ages, any chance of a discount on the 90 min 🙏
simulator_brief: Friendly regular. Will accept a polite no and book the 60 min, or ask the owner directly.
must: does not invent a loyalty discount
says it can pass the request to the owner OR states there are no current offers
offers to take her preferred day/time for the owner to confirm
must_not: confirms a booking as done (no system)
source: pattern seen in SalonGeek threads on regulars expecting discounts

title: Why are infills so expensive / do lashes last
facts: Classic infill (within 3 weeks) £35; full set £50; retention depends on natural lash cycle and aftercare (KB). No guarantee policy.
client_turns: why do infills cost £35 when my lashes fell out in 2 weeks anyway?? how long do they actually last
simulator_brief: Sceptical. Will ask 'so what's the point then'. Converts if answer is honest and aftercare is mentioned.
must: is honest that retention varies with natural lash cycle and aftercare
gives the infill price from facts
does not take it as a complaint unless the client says the last set was done at this salon and is unhappy
must_not: promises a fixed lifespan (e.g. '4 weeks guaranteed')
source: pattern seen in r/lashextensions retention complaints

title: New salon, price asked but KB empty

must: says it doesn't have the price to hand
offers to get the owner to confirm and asks one useful detail (e.g. hair length) OR takes contact preference
passes the question to owner
